figure.purpose: Large change chip at the top of the unit panel.

year.purpose: Current year in the year bar.

title.purpose: App name, sheet and popover titles (15-16px).

body-small.purpose: Addresses, filter options, toggles, About copy.

caption.purpose: Secondary lines, timeline years, tooltips; usually Mist Ink.

map-labels.purpose: Basemap labels use bundled Noto Sans glyph PBFs (Regular, Medium, Italic) so the map renders offline.

shadows.name: raised-segment

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one easing curve for all interface motion.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Segment, switch track and disclosure chevron transitions.

motion.name: pop
motion.purpose: Popover and About open: scale from 0.96 and 4px up; switch thumb travel.

motion.name: reflow
motion.purpose: Corner controls and year bar yield to the open panel.

motion.name: panel
motion.purpose: Unit panel slides in from the right (bottom sheet on phone).

motion.name: map-paint
motion.purpose: MapLibre style transition: heat cross-fade and badge settle.

motion.name: fly-to
motion.purpose: Map flies to a selected or searched unit, padded 420px clear of the panel.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: One ring pulse on units whose count rose in the year just stepped to.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All animations and transitions collapse under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Controls drop under search; unit panel becomes a 62vh bottom sheet.

provenance.heatImages: web/public/data/heat/<year>.png are generated by pipeline/heat.py from FEHD restaurant licence lists (DATA.GOV.HK, 2016-2026) geocoded with the Address Lookup Service; colour stops (the change ramp) and bounds are written to meta.json.
provenance.basemap: web/public/tiles/hk.pmtiles is a Protomaps extract of OpenStreetMap data (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), styled with @protomaps/basemaps flavours retuned in web/src/map/basemap.ts; attribution shown on the map.
provenance.glyphs: web/public/fonts holds Noto Sans glyph PBFs for basemap labels.
provenance.otherRasters: None. Icons are authored inline SVG; badges are drawn on canvas at runtime.

narrative.overview:
The map is the screen. A soft, warm-grey basemap fills the viewport edge to edge, and every interface element floats above it as a translucent glass card in the system face, the way a native map app does it. Nothing is invented for its own sake: the world is the category standard for map apps, chosen by the user over rolled directions, with Apple Maps as the craft bar. Its distinctiveness comes from one thing only: a five-step change ramp (grey, teal, amber, orange, red) that is the sole saturated colour anywhere on screen, carried identically by the map badges, the dots, the chips, the legend and the heat wash.

Density is map-app density: compact controls in the corners, a 14px body, one floating panel that slides in beside the live map rather than replacing it. Chrome is neutral ink on frosted white (or frosted graphite in dark mode); controls never borrow the ramp, so colour always means change frequency and nothing else. Motion is smooth and physical, a single long-tail ease used everywhere, with the map itself doing the largest moves (fly-to, heat cross-fade).

The build diverges from the direction contract in two small, deliberate places: the glass is 84% opaque rather than about 80%, and the top-left search is a 372px card holding the title line and a search field rather than a bare 380px pill. The build is the record.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed vector basemap (Protomaps extract of OpenStreetMap, served offline from a local PMTiles file), tuned pale so the ramp is the only saturated thing on screen.
Floating glass surfaces: frosted, hairline-bordered, one soft two-layer shadow, 14px corners.
System type only (SF Pro / PingFang HK); Chinese and English set side by side.
One five-step change ramp shared by canvas badges, map dots, chips, legend and the generated heat images.
Digits always carry the count; colour is never the only cue.
Light and dark schemes follow the operating system.

rules.name: The One Colour Rule
rules.body: The change ramp is the only saturated colour on screen. Chrome is ink on glass; the basemap is pale. If a new control needs emphasis, it gets ink, weight or position, never a hue.

rules.name: The Shared Ramp Rule
rules.body: Badges, dots, chips, the legend and the heat wash read from one ramp definition (and the pipeline's identical stop list). A step's colour never changes meaning between surfaces.

rules.name: The Digit Rule
rules.body: Every coloured count also shows its number. Colour supports the digit; it never replaces it.

rules.name: The System Face Rule
rules.body: All interface text is the platform's own UI face. No webfonts, no display face, no letter-spaced uppercase in the chrome.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change (counts, years, chips) uses tabular figures so it does not jitter while the year plays.

rules.name: The Map Stays Live Rule
rules.body: Nothing covers the map edge to edge except the compare sheet the user explicitly opens. Detail opens beside the map, and the controls move out of its way rather than under it.

rules.name: The One Float Rule
rules.body: There is one elevation for chrome. Popovers, panels, tooltips, sheets and buttons all use Float; nothing stacks a second, heavier shadow.

dos: Do take every hue that means "change" from the five-step ramp, and keep the heat pipeline's stop colours identical to it.
Do show the digit with every coloured count, in tabular figures.
Do float new chrome as a glass card: Frosted Glass, 22px blur at 180% saturation, 0.5px hairline, Float shadow, 14px radius.
Do emphasise controls with Graphite Ink (or near-white in dark mode), weight and placement.

Do move with the one ease (`cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`): 200ms for state, 220ms for popovers, 300–340ms for sheets and panels, 450ms for map paint cross-fades, 900ms for fly-to; collapse to 1ms under reduced motion.
Do keep the basemap pale and low-chroma so the ramp stays the loudest thing on screen; swap the zero step to Receding Slate on the dark map.
Do set Chinese and English side by side, Chinese first for sign names.
Do keep map labels above the heat wash.
donts: Don't colour buttons, toggles, links or selection states with a ramp step or any other hue.
Don't add a second typeface, a display face, or uppercase tracked labels to the interface chrome.
Don't wrap the map in sidebars of charts or KPI tiles; detail opens beside the live map.
Don't stack shadows or give one floating surface more elevation than another.
Don't use glyph or emoji icons; extend the authored 20px SVG set at 1.6px stroke.
Don't let badges overlap; resolve collisions by placing the higher count first.
